items.detail: Wall Street rebounded to close a wild July: the **S&P 500 rose 0.7% to 7,489.72**, the **Nasdaq climbed 1% to 25,373.85** and the **Dow added 276.97 points (0.53%) to 52,485.03**, with the Dow booking a **fourth straight winning month**.
items.why: A blowout Amazon cloud print reignited AI optimism and dragged the tape higher even as a sharp Apple selloff and climbing oil prices capped the gains.

items.detail: **Amazon soared ~15%** after Q2 revenue rose **20% to $200.6B** and **AWS grew 37% to $42.2B** — its fastest cloud expansion in 18 quarters — with management noting its AI and custom-chip units each cleared a **$25B annual run rate**.
items.why: Accelerating cloud and AI-chip revenue reframed Amazon's heavy AI capex as demand-driven, easing the same AI-spending fears that had whipsawed megacaps all week.

items.detail: **Apple plunged ~7.4% to $308.91**, shedding close to **$500B in market value**, even though fiscal Q3 revenue grew **16% to $109B** and iPhone sales jumped **22% to $54B**; it guided Q4 revenue up just **9–11%** versus the ~12.1% Street forecast.
items.why: Apple warned that component shortages and soaring costs from the AI data-center boom are straining its supply chain and squeezing margins, prompting an analyst downgrade in Tim Cook's final earnings as CEO.

items.detail: Oil extended its surge, with **Brent climbing above $88** and **WTI up more than 1% to about $84.67**, capping a monthly advance of **more than 20%**.
items.why: Iran said it attacked two tankers in the Strait of Hormuz while Houthi involvement grew and Saudi forces joined U.S. operations against Iran-backed groups in Iraq, keeping a war-driven inflation premium in crude.

items.detail: Attention now shifts to the week ahead, where fresh labor-market data and the aftermath of last week's hawkish 9–3 Fed hold will test whether the Amazon-led rebound can hold against a still-elevated **30-year yield** and a >20% monthly oil spike.
Indian equities edged higher Friday, with the **Sensex near 78,000** and the **Nifty holding above 24,350**, extending Wednesday's rebound into a modest but positive weekly finish.
items.why: Positive global cues from Amazon's cloud blowout and steady domestic buying offset a hostile backdrop of higher U.S. yields and firmer oil.

items.detail: Domestic institutions did the heavy lifting: **DIIs were net buyers of ₹2,260.4 crore** while **FIIs bought a modest ₹277.5 crore** in the cash segment, keeping benchmarks supported despite global volatility.
items.why: Robust DII inflows cushioned the market as foreign investors stayed cautious amid a spike in U.S. Treasury yields and renewed oil-price risk.

items.detail: The leadership flipped from Wednesday: **IT was the biggest drag, sliding more than 2%**, and FMCG lagged, while **auto and financials led** the advance.
items.why: Indian software gave back part of its recent bargain-hunting rally as global tech sentiment turned choppy, rotating buying into rate-sensitive autos and financials.

items.detail: The renewed oil rally is now the market's chief overhang, with **Brent back above $88** and its monthly gain topping **20%** as the Strait of Hormuz threat intensifies.
items.why: As a major net crude importer, India faces a heavier import bill, rupee pressure and inflation risk whenever oil sustains above $90, eroding a tailwind the market had enjoyed for weeks.

items.detail: **Bitcoin is trading near $62,865** entering August, having failed to reclaim the upper boundary of its descending channel after ending July under renewed selling pressure.
items.why: Last week's hawkish Fed hold and the jump in Treasury yields kept risk appetite subdued, leaving BTC unable to confirm a bullish breakout.

items.detail: **Ether is trading near $1,865**, slipping below the rising trendline that had supported its July recovery as the broader sector stays defensive.
items.why: Higher-beta majors continue to underperform Bitcoin as elevated yields and lingering macro risk push traders to trim exposure across the risk curve.

items.detail: Spot Bitcoin ETFs limped to the finish, pulling in just **~$205M of net inflows in July — the smallest monthly total on record**, as a $999M inflow streak from July 14–22 was largely undone by roughly **$526M of outflows** over the following four sessions.
items.why: Institutional demand has turned anemic and hedging-driven, following $2.43B of May outflows and $4.52B in June, leaving ETF flows a fragile swing factor amid macro stress.

items.detail: Sentiment remains fragile with the **Fear & Greed Index stuck at 28 ('Fear')**, and analysts flag a **hidden liquidation wall near $39,900** as a downside risk if selling accelerates.
items.why: The combination of a still-hawkish Fed and a re-escalating Hormuz-region oil shock keeps speculative capital cautious and leverage vulnerable to a cascade.

crossCuttingTheme: AI-capex was the market's fault line this week: Amazon's 37% AWS surge validated the AI spend and drove a broad megacap rebound, while Apple's supply-chain warning showed the same data-center boom straining hardware — even as Brent above $88 on the Strait of Hormuz conflict revived an inflation premium that pressured Indian IT, kept the Fed hawkish and left crypto defensive.
